title: Can anybody get environments looking good?
author: Odd_Zookeepergame915
selftext: I've been having a blast making my UE5 arena shooter with AI. But for some reason it really sucks with environments. It's like it'll place things but it's so procedurally generated. Has anybody had any luck with making environments or prompts to help? I'm not trying to make something photo realistic but at least something that just doesn't seem like things are just scattered everywhere.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: ai is bad at this bc it doesnt know why stuff goes where, so it just sprinkles. for an arena shooter id greybox the layout yourself first (lanes, cover, sightlines, spawns) and only let the ai dress it after. UE5's PCG framework helps too, you give it rules like stay off paths, cluster near walls, thin out with distance, instead of asking it to drop props one by one. also tell it to place stuff in groups, crates stacked against a wall, debris around something broken, not single items. what's the setting, sci fi? industrial?

replies.author: Odd_Zookeepergame915
replies.body:
Honestly it takes a lot of inspiration from call of duty but then a mixture of fun like a Roblox game I like to play (I'm 42 don't judge LOL). I play a lot of FPS shooters over the years so I just want something that's fun and chill to play when you get home from work. I've got a lot of stuff done. Just trying to get these little small details. 

I appreciate the input! I think I might try to gray boxing myself route so maybe it gets an idea of what I'm trying to do and improves.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: 42 and building a cod x roblox hybrid is a way better midlife crisis than a sports car 😂 one thing that helps once the greybox is in: give the ai the why for each area, like 'this is a sniper lane, low cover only, keep sightlines open' instead of 'make a warehouse'. it sprinkles way less random junk when it knows what the space is for.

replies.author: Odd_Zookeepergame915
replies.body: Shit you ain't lying man. It does take a lot of time up so sometimes I got to take a break and be like go back to life LOL. But it's so much fun just telling AI what to do. Things used to take me days or weeks to learn..

comments.author: Chinoui67
comments.body: I use ai to make me devtools to  fix environmment ! Working on its basis. Or screenshotting and drawing on it directly

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body:
If you really don't want to hand place things yourself, one thing you can try is telling Claude/whatever AI you're using, to look at the scene from a realistic perspective and determine what types of assets belong together with the terrain. Look up reference images online and research what would make a realistic/pleasing scene to look at. 

There are a lot of ways that can be worded, this is a very simple way. If you're using Claude, tell Claude what issue you're having with asset placement and give it a prompt similar to what I wrote, and ask it to come up with a gameplan for how things should be placed. 

It might not get you all the way there, but it can help a lot
